issue.title: 4.6: Align remaining docs (README version, license, website sentence, CLAUDE architecture)
issue.body_excerpt: Run doc-manager for README, privacy-policy, CLAUDE architecture bullets. License: pick MIT vs proprietary and make package.json, README, and CLAUDE agree.

affected_files.role: primary - 'Status' section line 360-364 says 'Current Version: 1.1.0' but package.json/manifest.json are 1.2.0. License section line 350-352 says 'Proprietary and confidential' but CLAUDE.md line 6 says 'Open source: MIT licensed'. Pick one (MIT per CLAUDE.md) and make all three agree. README also lacks the 'no implementation yet' style architecture bullets (none present) — fine, no change there.

primary - 'license: UNLICENSED' (line 41) is inconsistent with both CLAUDE.md (MIT) and README.md (Proprietary). Pick one license and set it. Acceptance: 'License string is identical in README and package.json'.

primary - line 6 says 'Open source: MIT licensed' but README says 'Proprietary' and package.json says UNLICENSED. Also, the 'Current Project Status' (line 453-463) says 'Phase: Pre — agent environment' and 'Baseline: RED' but the extension IS shipped (content script, SW, dashboard) — the issue says the line must not say 'no implementation yet'. Current text already says 'The extension implementation is shipped' so that specific phrase is fine, but the stale 'Pre — agent environment' / 'RED baseline' claim IS out of date. Rewrite the Current Project Status to reflect that the extension is shipped and P4 is the active phase.

secondary - line 4 says 'The extension has no backend and no accompanying website' but a landing page exists at landing-page/index.html. Either drop the 'no accompanying website' phrase or rephrase (e.g. 'The extension has no backend; the marketing landing page is static HTML at echo-footprint.luongnv.com').

analysis.current_implementation: Four files, four different versions of the truth. package.json: version=1.2.0, license=UNLICENSED. manifest.json: version=1.2.0. README.md: 'Current Version: 1.1.0', 'License: Proprietary and confidential'. CLAUDE.md: 'Open source: MIT licensed' AND 'Phase: Pre — agent environment' (stale). privacy-policy.md: 'no accompanying website' (stale — landing page exists).
analysis.limitations: Version drift is the canonical P4 doc-alignment finding. License disagreement across three files is a legal-distribution hazard. Stale project-status text misleads every new contributor and every AI agent that opens the repo.
analysis.change_surface: 4 files, all text-only. (1) Pick the canonical license: project is dual-licensed, not yet settled — recommendation is 'MIT' (matches CLAUDE.md and the OSS nature of the repo, and the privacy-policy already implies it's open). (2) Bump README to 'Current Version: 1.2.0' and rewrite the License section to 'MIT — see LICENSE file'. (3) Add a LICENSE file (MIT, standard text) if not present — `ls LICENSE` is needed to confirm. (4) Update CLAUDE.md 'Current Project Status' to 'Phase: P4 (Polish) — extension shipped; final perf/UX/doc alignment' and drop the 'RED baseline' / 'Pre' phrasing. (5) Update privacy-policy.md to drop the 'no accompanying website' claim or qualify it.
analysis.root_cause: Three independent doc files (README, CLAUDE, package.json) drifted from each other as the project moved from a planning document into a shipped extension. The version, license, and status fields were each updated in only one of the three files.

options.name: Pick MIT, align all four files
options.summary: Add LICENSE (MIT) at repo root. Set package.json license to MIT. README 'Status' version 1.2.0; 'License' section to MIT. CLAUDE.md 'Current Project Status' to P4 shipped. privacy-policy.md 'no backend and no accompanying website' to 'no backend; the marketing landing page is static HTML'.
pros: Aligns three out-of-date files with the truth
MIT matches the existing CLAUDE.md claim and the OSS posture of the repo
cons: License choice is a one-way decision; requires the maintainer to confirm MIT
options.risk_details: Text-only changes. The license decision is the only thing requiring a human in the loop. Verify: `rg -n 'MIT' LICENSE README.md package.json CLAUDE.md` shows 4 matches; `rg -n 'UNLICENSED|Proprietary' README.md package.json CLAUDE.md` exits 1.

options.name: Pick Proprietary, align all four files
options.summary: Same as Option 1 but flip to Proprietary. Drop the MIT from CLAUDE.md, set README and package.json to Proprietary. No LICENSE file.
pros: Matches what was previously shipped in README
cons: The repo is publicly developed and the project description (package.json) calls out 'privacy-first' — Proprietary is the wrong choice for an OSS project

options_rejected: Proprietary — contradicts the project's public, OSS posture and the existing CLAUDE.md claim

decision_record.root_cause: package.json (UNLICENSED), README (Proprietary), and CLAUDE (MIT) disagree on license; README version is 1.1.0 while package.json/manifest are 1.2.0; CLAUDE Current Project Status still says 'Pre — agent environment / RED baseline' even though the extension is shipped; privacy-policy claims 'no accompanying website' even though a landing page exists.
decision_record.selected_option: MIT, align all four files (add LICENSE)
decision_record.residual_risk: The license choice needs maintainer confirmation before the PR is merged. If the maintainer prefers a different license (e.g. Apache-2.0), only the three license strings need to change; the structural cleanup is unchanged.
